# Trends Explore

*Tool* · also written Google Trends Explore · Explore page

The Google Trends page for comparing search terms and topics over time, by region and with related queries.

Narrative: the topic [Google Trends tools and features](../topics/trends-features.md) tells the story; this card lists what links to it.

14 claims mention it: 13 shown or said at the event (5 not in Google docs, 5 confirmed by Google docs, 3 consistent with Google docs), 1 press report. A card is a map: cite the claim ids, with the citation given after each claim.

## Google's documentation

Documented in: [Compare Trends search terms](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/4359550?hl=en), [Understanding How the Google Trends Explore Page uses Gemini models](https://support.google.com/trends/answer/16763742?hl=en).

## Shown or said at the event

Not in Google's documentation first: present those as said at Search Central Live, never as documented policy.

- [`D2-C763`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: The legacy Google Trends Explore page is still available but will be retired: Google is adding its features to the new Explore page until everyone can move to the new one (no date was given). `[D2-C763, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C769`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: A Google Trends Explore chart presented on stage put worldwide search interest in Gemini above ChatGPT for the first time ever in September 2025, during a sharp surge for Gemini. `[D2-C769, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C778`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: A Google Trends engineer found the cause of the 2012 'ai' spike by zooming in on that time range on the Explore page and reading the related queries. `[D2-C778, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C813`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: Google said colour maps of the geographic breakdown of search interest (regions within a country, or countries worldwide) had launched in the new Google Trends Explore page about a month before the October 2026 talk. `[D2-C813, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C815`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, not in Google docs: The category filter of the legacy Google Trends Explore page has been reintroduced in the new Explore page. `[D2-C815, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C760`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google Trends has two flagship experiences: the Explore page and Trending now. `[D2-C760, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C762`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: Google launched a brand-new Google Trends Explore page at the beginning of 2026. `[D2-C762, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C790`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: For keyword selection, Google recommended entering candidate keywords on the Google Trends Explore page, setting the relevant country, region and time frame, and seeing which terms have the higher search interest. `[D2-C790, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C798`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: For scheduling, Google recommended checking on the Google Trends Explore page whether the topics relevant to your domain show seasonality; many topics do, though not all. `[D2-C798, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C806`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, confirmed by Google docs: The new Google Trends Explore page has a 'Suggest search terms' button that opens an optional Gemini-based side panel. `[D2-C806, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C761`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The Google Trends Explore page, which Google called the heart of Trends, shows search interest in a query or topic and how it changes over time. `[D2-C761, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C794`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: The 'Commonly searched queries' section of the new Google Trends Explore page, called related queries in the legacy Explore page, lists queries that people typed in the same search sessions as the entered term. `[D2-C794, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`
- [`D2-C811`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Stage, Day 2, consistent with Google docs: Quick comparisons, a recent Google Trends Explore page feature, show year-over-year, month-over-month and week-over-week comparisons as chips when a single search term or topic is entered. `[D2-C811, stage, Omri Weisman, Day 2]`

## Press reports

- [`D2-C816`](../sessions/D2-S24-google-trends.md) Press: Search Engine Roundtable reported on 2 September 2026 that Google had announced category filters for the new Google Trends Explore page, usable with or without a query. `[D2-C816, press, Search Engine Roundtable (2 September 2026), https://www.seroundtable.com/google-trends-filter-category-42007.html]`
